title: On Mixing the colours by hand
subtitle: 社区社会 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 社区社会（社会服务与人际沟通·社区与社会参与）
meta: 主题语境：社区社会（社会服务与人际沟通·社区与社会参与）　|　核心词汇：mix　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 mix 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1972 the tailor ① mixed the colours by hand with great care, and every customer in the shop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the tailor ② mixes the colours by hand on the same day without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ mix the colours by hand at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ mixed the colours by hand before — a line in the order for November 1966 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Mixing the colours by hand with great care, the tailor said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the needle at the far mirror, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ mix with the village boys easily on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Mix with the village boys easily at once and never mention it again.

By 1979 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the order, and a new customer from the next shop ⑧ mixes with the village boys easily with great care every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the mirror, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ mixed the colours by hand again when nobody else would.

⑩ To mix the colours by hand, my mother said in 1984, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the shop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the shop forgets, somebody mixes the colours by hand on the same day again and somebody must mix the colours by hand with great care all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 混合（一般过去式 mixed the colours by hand：1972 年裁缝头一回这样做，小心翼翼地）
B. v. 混合（一般现在 mixes the colours by hand：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 混合（不定式 to mix the colours by hand：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 混合（过去完成时 had mixed the colours by hand：1966 年十一月的订单簿上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 混合（动名词 mixing the colours by hand 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 相处（mix with the village boys easily：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去相处和村里的孩子很容易相处）
G. v. 相处（mix with the village boys easily：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 混合（后段两处：新来的顾客照例 mixes with the village boys easily，而母亲又一次 mixed the colours by hand）

items.q: to mix the colours by hand
mixed the colours by hand before

to mix the colours by hand

answers.why: mix 意为“混合”，1972 年裁缝小心翼翼地混合用手工调那些颜色，那是裁缝铺里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 mixed。
mix 意为“混合”，自那以后裁缝当天就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 mixes。
mix 意为“混合”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯混合用手工调那些颜色”，此处为不定式 to mix the colours by hand。
mix 意为“混合”，订单簿里 十一月 那行字说明早在 1979 年之前就有人混合过，故用过去完成时 had mixed。
mix 意为“混合”，裁缝说“混合用手工调那些颜色这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 mixing the colours by hand 作主语。
mix 意为“相处”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去相处和村里的孩子很容易相处”，should ever 之后用原形 mix with the village boys easily。
mix 意为“相处”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻相处和村里的孩子很容易相处（mix with the village boys easily at once），以后再也不要提起。
mix 意为“混合”，新来的顾客每个星期都照例相处和村里的孩子很容易相处，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 mixes。
mix 意为“混合”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次小心翼翼地混合用手工调那些颜色，用一般过去式 mixed 叙述。
mix 意为“混合”，结尾那句是母亲 1984 年的话：要混合用手工调那些颜色，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和裁缝铺记住的那一件。

多年以后，裁缝仍当天就做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（mixes the colours by hand）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯混合用手工调那些颜色这件事本身。（to mix the colours by hand）
早在 1966 年就有人混合用手工调那些颜色，十一月那天订单簿上的一行字就是证据。（had mixed the colours by hand）
裁缝说过，小心翼翼地混合用手工调那些颜色这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（mixing the colours by hand 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻相处和村里的孩子很容易相处，以后再也不要提起。（mix with the village boys easily，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 mix 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1972 the tailor mixed the colours by hand with great care, and nobody in the shop forgot it.
Even now the tailor mixes the colours by hand on the same day whenever the shop asks.
Mixing the colours by hand with great care, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever mix with the village boys easily on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new customer from the next shop mixes with the village boys easily with great care every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother mixed the colours by hand again, and the shop remembered that half.
